Ann (Customer): hitting high latency on /v1/generate. request_id=abcd-1234-ef56 seen at 2024-06-15T14:02:12Z. Response took ~12s. Can you check server logs?

Oliver (Support): sorry about that — can you share the curl repro and confirm the request_id? also a ~5min time window helps. if possible please generate a debug bundle.

Ann (Customer): request_id: abcd-1234-ef56. minimal curl:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-large\",\"input\":\"short prompt\",\"request_id\":\"abcd-1234-ef56\"}'
```
Happened at 2024-06-15T14:02:12Z. thanks.

Oliver (Support): thanks — i'm going to search logs now. SRE — Liam, can you check infra for that req id? query i'll run below.

Liam (SRE): running KQL on logs cluster:
```kql
@timestamp >= \"2024-06-15T13:57:00Z\" and @timestamp <= \"2024-06-15T14:07:00Z\" and request_id == \"abcd-1234-ef56\"
```
If nothing shows, check archived indices (logs-archive-*). retention window for hot indices is 30 days; beyond that we need an archive restore (file a ticket). also please include trace_id if available.

Oliver (Support): debug bundle instructions:
```bash
redwood-cli collect-debug --request-id abcd-1234-ef56 --out debug-abcd.tar.gz
```
or Console > Support > Collect debug (https://console.redwood.ai/support).

debug-bot: Debug bundle available: https://console.redwood.ai/support/bundles/DBG-20240615-0001
